GULBARGA IN MVC NO.479/2011, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

The North-East Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (henceforth referred as 'Corporation') has filed this appeal challenging the liability fixed on it to pay the compensation awarded by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.479/2011,
vide judgment and award dated 03.11.2014.
2. The impugned judgment and award discloses that the claimant was travelling in a bus belonging to the Corporation on 01.06.2008 from Gangavathi to Shorapur.
It is alleged that the driver of the bus drove it in a rash and negligent manner due to which the bus fishtailed and its rear portion dashed against a lorry.

The claimant who was sitting on the right side on the rear of the bus NC:
2023:KHC-K:1364 sustained injuries on the right hand and she was shifted to Government General Hospital, Shorapur.
She was thereafter shifted to Kekare Accident Hospital at Pune, where she was admitted as an inpatient.
It was diagnosed that the claimant had suffered fracture of right humerus and fracture of right elbow.

The claimant claimed that she was a tailor and was earning Rs.40,000/-
per annum and due to the injuries, she was disabled from undertaking any tailoring work.

Hence,
she filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- from the Corporation.

3. The claim petition was opposed by the Corporation which contended that it was the driver of the lorry who was negligent and a charge sheet was filed against the driver of the said lorry and therefore, the Corporation was not liable to pay any compensation.

It generally denied the accident,
age and occupation of the claimant.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and she marked Exs.P1 to P21.
She also examined a doctor as PW.2, who assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 80% to the right upper limb.
She also examined a witness who shifted her to the hospital as PW.3.
The Corporation examined one of its officials as RW.1, who apparently was not driving the bus at the time of the accident.
5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation.
It held that the claimant had suffered fracture of right humerus and right elbow.

It assessed the disability suffered by the The Managing Director vs Smt.Sangeetha W/O.Devendra on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122068259/
2
claimant at 10% to the whole body and her income was notionally considered at Rs.3,000/- per month and the following compensation was awarded:

NC: 2023:KHC-K:1364 Towards pain and suffering Rs.30,000/- Towards loss of amenities Rs.10,000/-
and enjoyment in life Towards loss of future Rs.57,600/-
income Towards medical expenses Rs.1,80,992/-
& incident charges Towards attendant's Rs.25,000/-
charges, food nourishment and conveyance expenses Towards loss of income Rs.9,000/-
during period of treatment Total Rs.3,12,592/-
6.
The Corporation was directed to pay the compensating along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the Corporation is in appeal.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant/Corporation contended that the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the lorry thereby indicating that he was negligent and was responsible for the accident and therefore, no claim could be made against the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1364 Corporation.
He also contended that the claimant had filed a private complaint as per Ex.P2 giving the details of the lorry which caused the accident and the police filed a 'C' report.

He therefore contended that the documents indicated that the claimant too accepted that it was the driver of the lorry who was negligent and therefore, the owner and insurer of the lorry were responsible to indemnify the claimant.

8. The learned counsel for the respondent/claimant submits that even though a private complaint was filed which was referred to the jurisdictional police for investigation, the police have filed a 'C' report indicating thereby that they were unable to trace the accused.
He therefore submits that the claimant is entitled to pursue the claim petition against the Corporation which was one of the tortfeasors.
9. The fact that two vehicles were involved in the accident is not in dispute.

The claimant was travelling in the bus belonging to the Corporation and she suffered NC:
2023:KHC-K:1364 injuries in the road accident.

The claimant was therefore entitled to proceed against any of the tortfeasor under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
The Managing Director vs Smt.Sangeetha W/O.Devendra on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122068259/
3 1988.
The Tribunal after considering the material on record rightly held that the claimant is entitled to pursue her remedy against any of the tortfeasors.
Consequently, this Court does not see any error in application of law or appreciating the facts and awarding compensation.
10. In that view of the matter, this appeal lacks merit and is dismissed.
Any amount deposited by the appellant/Corporation is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
